chapters.title: Growing up on Ravine Street
chapters.summary: The third of six children, raised above her father's shoe repair shop. Walked to St. Brigid's every morning, often late.

anecdotes.text: She once traded a week of dish duty for her brother's roller skates, then wore them until the wheels gave out.
A draft note about the shoe shop that the family has not reviewed yet.

openQuestions: What was the name of the shoe shop?
Did she finish high school in 1956?

chapters.title: The house on Linden
chapters.summary: Married Bill in 1961. Four children. The kitchen table was the centre of everything, including other people's problems.

anecdotes.text: Every Sunday she cooked for ten whether or not ten people were coming. Somebody always came.

openQuestions: Which year did they move to Linden Avenue?

toneNotes: Warm and plain-spoken, with dry humour. She would have hated anything flowery. Short sentences suit her.
coveragePhotoGaps: No photos from the 1940s childhood years
Very few photos of Peggy with her grandchildren
